title: dream comes true
author: Glittering_Lime_4777
selftext: personally, i think the best part of ai game dev is not for making commercial games that puts millions into your bank account, but watching the dream game in your brain finally comes true, I always imagine a cute little pistol clearing floors of enemies using his own recoil, but I can never make my imagination come to life due to how frustrating it is for me to code, with ai, I can finally see the pistol shooting blobs and cutely ascend to the next floor which without ai, it takes much more efforts to learn and achieve. I hope people give less hate to ai and appreciate how it can visualize our creative ideas with ease

comments.author: w1zinvestmentss
comments.body: This looks great. I agree, the beauty of AI is that it gives everyone a chance to create. Especially the ones who are passionate about something, no more gatekeepers or begging other to build your vision. It will take a while but we will see some cool things from passionate people. It also lets you explore ideas that you would never explore.

replies.author: BattlersNetwork
replies.body:
I like this reply better. The others made me assume you might have been closed-minded and I am not fond of preaching to deaf ears. 

Time is a currency, friend. Time must be spent to learn a new skill, to refine the skill, and to apply the skill. Coding itself, nevermind making a whole game, is very expensive time wise. 

Unfortunately, those experiencing poverty need to expend more of their Time just to live. That means spending extra Time for extra hours at work and for multiple jobs. Spending extra Time trying to find the cheapest groceries, or one's self or dependants go hungry. Spending extra time on the phone trying to get bills reduced, payment dates extended, or looking for any sort of benefits at all. Spending Time dealing with the mental disorders which may manifest from experiencing these stresses. 

This isnt even close to a quarter of what poverty does to an individual, and we are only speaking of Time being gatekept here. 

The availablity of technology is not a sound argument either, friend. How can anyone with a smartphone and access to AI be handicapped from learning a skill in any way? Well I can personally take a houseless person about a block and a half from my place to a little yellow tent where they will be assigned a smartphone from the government with the capabilities to handle ChatGPT. And I am going to assume you would not be asking this same houseless person 'What is stopping you from learning to code if you have the luxuries of a smartphone and AI?'. This is an extreme case, yes, but the point stands. The access to technology is no longer a status symbol which represents freedom of time and choice as it did in the past.

So yes, despite what anyone believes, poverty gatekeeps individuals in one of the worse ways imaginable on this planet. And I will double down and call you and all those who are unaware of its effects blessed.

comments.author: snezna_kraljica
comments.body: Creative ideas come from restriction and learning. It's a fundamental part of it. Iconic characters like Mario stem from the fact that there just was a 16x16px grid and you had to think really hard and try so much stuff until you got it right. If AI is in just solving all your ideas directly I think you're missing out a lot of the good stuff that comes from learning and a challenge.
